title.en: Solid shapes: faces, edges and corners (additional, not in the textbook)

text.en: Children made animal and bird faces on old boxes, cans and bottles. A pig face on a cube, a puppy on a cylinder and a cat on a cuboid, a bird with a pointed beak on a cone.

Welcome to Toy Joy. Today we meet solid shapes. Solid shapes are the shapes of things we can hold, like boxes, cans and balls.
A cube is like a dice. All its faces are flat squares of the same size.
A cuboid is like a box or a brick. Its faces are flat, and a cube is a special kind of cuboid.
A cylinder is like a can or a bottle. It has two flat faces and one curved face.
A cone is like an ice cream cone or a joker's cap. It has one flat face, one curved face and a pointed tip.
A sphere is like a ball. It has only a curved surface, no flat face and no edge.
The flat or curved surface of a solid is called a face. Where two faces meet we get an edge, and where edges meet we get a corner.
Some edges are straight and some are curved. A cylinder has curved edges, a cube has straight edges.
Use old boxes, cans and bottles for craft work. Join shapes to build houses, towers and rockets, and say which shapes you used.

problem.en: Jaya built a rocket with 1 cone on top, 2 cylinders and 1 cuboid. How many shapes did she use?

text.en: Count the cone: 1.
Add 2 cylinders and 1 cuboid.
1 + 2 + 1 = 4 shapes.

prompt.en: A friend says a ball is a cube. What will you say?

requiredIdeas.en: A cube has flat square faces and corners
A sphere has no flat face

points.en: Cube, cuboid, cylinder, cone and sphere are solid shapes.
Faces, edges and corners describe a solid.
A sphere has only a curved surface.
